title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a table of contents for the later parts of an expanded EGA plan. It covers the methods of construction of moduli and representing schemes, with no mathematics carried out on the page.

C) Projective methods of construction:
- §14 Bounded (limited) families.
- §15 Hilbert functors and Hilbert schemes, plus the Quot scheme ('celui aux quotients').
- §16 Picard functors and Picard schemes. The note says this section is restricted to existence theorems obtained by projective methods. It also proposes the analogous problem for commutative affine group schemes more general than G_m: representability of the functor of G-torsors H^1(X/S, G) for commutative affine G.
- §17 Variants of Picard.
- §18 Applications to curves (Jacobians).
- §19 Formalism of norms (norm maps for finite locally free morphisms, used to build Pic and Hilbert-type quotients).
- §20 Mumford's multiprojective invariants, i.e. GIT quotients in a multi-projective setting as used for Picard and moduli.

D) Mixed methods of construction:
- §21 Representability of Pic, Pic^0 and Pic^τ. This includes Mumford's argument that uses GIT (§20).
- §22 Representability of functors such as Π_{X/Y} (Weil restriction / Hom and Aut functors) over S, via theorems 'of Matsumura type'. This refers to Matsumura–Oort (1967) on representability of group functors such as Aut_X.

A NB states the prerequisites assumed: topologies, faithfully flat descent and quotient sheaves, presumably as treated in an earlier chapter ('Ch. V'?).

A list of 'Manquent' (items still missing) follows:
- In the chapter on group schemes: the theorems on abelian varieties (VA), and the general finiteness theorems on Picard.
- In the chapter on Picard:
  - the general study (specialization?) of Picard schemes, including a Mumford criterion;
  - (?) a study of Pic of a projective scheme via a pencil of hyperplane sections;
  - the theorems on Picard of the 'certain equivalences' type (algebraic / numerical / τ-equivalence, as in FGA Exp. 236 and SGA 6 XIII).
- In the chapter on π_1: van Kampen-type descent formulations in terms of fundamental groups (cf. SGA 1 IX).

The page serves to organize the planned treatment of FGA-style representability theorems (Hilbert, Quot, Picard) inside EGA.
errors: No mathematical claims to check; it is a plan. Section numbers were renumbered on the page (17→18, 18→19, 20→21 etc.), so cross-references like '§20' in §21 refer to the renumbered GIT section.

missed.claim: Grothendieck planned to treat Picard-type representability for commutative affine group schemes beyond G_m inside the same projective framework as Pic. This is only partially systematized in the later literature.
missed.quote: également le cas de groupes affines commutatifs plus général que G_m
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest: moduli of torsors under commutative affine groups are studied piecemeal (μ_n, tori, generalized Jacobians). A unified treatment was intended but never written.

missed.claim: Planned study of Pic of a projective scheme in terms of a pencil of hyperplane sections, marked with a question mark.
missed.quote: Étude de Picard d'un schéma projectif en termes d'un pinceau de sections hyperplanes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low: a Lefschetz-pencil approach to Pic is classical in spirit. It is merely a planned item.

deep.surprise_reason: A plan of EGA chapters on construction methods (Hilbert, Picard, GIT, Matsumura-type representability). It documents intended scope, including the integration of Mumford's GIT and Matsumura–Oort. All topics are well known; there are only minor unrealized items.
transcription_corrections: 'les ths relatifs aux UA' is more likely 'aux VA' (variétés abéliennes).

'O V' in the NB is probably a chapter reference such as 'Ch. V'. The NB reads roughly: 'On suppose connues toutes les gén. fondamentales (topologies, descente fid. plate, faisceaux quotients); i.e. celles au besoin dans Ch. V'.
'[-publication-] {+publication+} générale des schémas de Picard' is uncertain; the word may be 'spécialisation' or similar.
In §16 the parenthesis likely reads '(Ths d'existence projectifs exclusivement; également le cas de groupes affines commutatifs plus généraux que G_m...)'.
Section renumbering: originally §17 Applications aux courbes, §18 Formalisme des normes, §20 Mumford, §20 Pic. These were corrected to 18, 19, 20 and 21, and §21 refers to §20.
